sourcedFrom: EAA Windicator Series Double Action Revolver — Warnings and Instruction Manual — Warnings and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) (cached from a 2015 capture; the document is undated on its face)
cleanIntro: A double-action swing-out revolver, and EAA's cleaning procedure is short because the gun does not come apart: cylinder out, clean, oil, done. ⛔ Two things here are EAA's own. The cylinder latch is pushed FORWARD to open — the Smith & Wesson direction, not the Colt one — and EAA warns specifically against over-oiling, because trapped powder and dust congeal into deposits that interfere with the action. ⚠ EAA also states this revolver has an internal safety and does not require an empty chamber under the hammer, and then recommends leaving one empty anyway.

steps.title: Two hands, barrel DOWN, then the latch forward
steps.action: Use both hands so nothing falls. Point the barrel down, push the cylinder latch FORWARD and push the cylinder out of the frame to the left.
steps.prose: Barrel down while the cylinder swings out means a loose round drops clear of the action instead of into it. Fingers stay out of the trigger guard the whole time.
steps.quote: Open the cylinder by pushing the cylinder latch forward and pushing the cylinder out of the frame. See Figure 22.
steps.cite: EAA Windicator Series Double Action Revolver — Warnings and Instruction Manual — Warnings and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — TO UNLOAD AND/OR EXTRACT EMPTY CASES, printed p.13
steps.warn: Keep your fingers out of the trigger guard and off the trigger.

steps.title: Barrel UP, hand behind the cylinder, then eject
steps.action: Now turn the barrel up, cup one hand behind the cylinder, and push the ejector rod to throw the cases out into your hand. Then look through every chamber.
steps.prose: Down to open, up to eject — the two directions are doing different jobs and swapping them is how cases fall back into the chambers as the rod returns.
steps.quote: Cupping one hand behind the cylinder, point the barrel up and push the ejector rod to eject the cartridges/empty cases from the chambers of the cylinder. See Figure 23.
steps.cite: EAA Windicator Series Double Action Revolver — Warnings and Instruction Manual — Warnings and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — TO UNLOAD AND/OR EXTRACT EMPTY CASES, printed p.13

steps.title: If the hammer is cocked, decock it under thumb control
steps.action: Both hands dry. Hold the frame firmly forward of the trigger guard with your off hand so it carries the weight. Thumb firmly on the hammer spur, squeeze the trigger only enough for the hammer to break free, then let it down slowly under your thumb to rest against the frame.
steps.prose: The off hand carrying the weight is the part that makes this safe — it frees the shooting hand to do nothing but control the hammer and the trigger. Practise it empty first; EAA says so explicitly.
steps.aside: The key to safe decocking is having the weight of the revolver controlled with one hand, while the thumb and forefinger of the "shooting hand" control the hammer and trigger.
steps.quote: Place your right thumb firmly on the hammer spur. With your thumb securely in control of the hammer, squeeze the trigger only enough to permit the hammer to break free of the trigger.
steps.cite: EAA Windicator Series Double Action Revolver — Warnings and Instruction Manual — Warnings and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — DECOCKING, printed p.17

steps.title: What you need, and the cylinder stays swung out
steps.action: Leave the cylinder swung out for the whole job. You need a cleaning rod, cotton bore patches, a brass bore brush, powder solvent, a small soft brush and good gun oil.
steps.prose: That list is EAA's and it is worth taking literally on one point: a BRASS bore brush, not steel. The rest is an ordinary revolver kit.
steps.quote: Materials needed to clean this revolver are: a cleaning rod, cotton bore patches, brass bore brush, powder solvent, a small soft brush and good quality gun oil.
steps.cite: EAA Windicator Series Double Action Revolver — Warnings and Instruction Manual — Warnings and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — TO CLEAN AND MAINTAIN YOUR REVOLVER, printed pp.18-19

steps.title: Bore and every chamber with the brush and solvent
steps.action: Scrub the bore and all the chambers with the bore brush and powder solvent to take out powder and lead residue.
steps.prose: EAA writes it as one instruction covering both, and on a .357 the chambers matter as much as the bore — a chamber fouled from a diet of .38 Special will make .357 cases stick hard.
steps.quote: Using the bore brush with powder solvent, scrub the interior of the barrels and chambers to remove any powder and lead residue in the bore.
steps.cite: EAA Windicator Series Double Action Revolver — Warnings and Instruction Manual — Warnings and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — TO CLEAN AND MAINTAIN YOUR REVOLVER, printed pp.18-19

steps.title: Fouling on the firing wall, the barrel and the frame
steps.action: Take the powder fouling off the firing wall behind the cylinder, off the rear face of the barrel and the front of the cylinder, with the small soft brush and solvent.
steps.prose: The blast ring on the cylinder face and the recoil shield behind it is where a revolver actually gets dirty, and letting it build closes up the cylinder gap until the gun binds.
steps.quote: Any powder fouling on the firing wall, barrel, etc. can be easily cleaned with a brush and powder solvent.
steps.cite: EAA Windicator Series Double Action Revolver — Warnings and Instruction Manual — Warnings and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — TO CLEAN AND MAINTAIN YOUR REVOLVER, printed pp.18-19

steps.title: ⛔ Wipe the solvent OFF before the oil goes on
steps.action: Wipe away all the excess solvent, then oil. Do not leave solvent standing on the finish.
steps.prose: ⛔ EAA gives the reason: prolonged or excess contact with solvent damages the bluing. This is a blued gun with a thin finish, and the damage is cosmetic right up until it becomes rust.
steps.quote: USE CAUTION while using solvents in gun bore cleaning. Prolonged or excess contact with solvents can damage the gun's bluing and finish.
steps.cite: EAA Windicator Series Double Action Revolver — Warnings and Instruction Manual — Warnings and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — TO CLEAN AND MAINTAIN YOUR REVOLVER, printed pp.18-19

steps.title: Oil the bore LAST, and go light on the outside
steps.action: Finish by swabbing the bore and chambers with a cotton patch carrying gun oil, then wipe all the external surfaces with a light coat of rust preventative. ⛔ Light — not generous.
steps.prose: ⛔ EAA names the failure exactly: too much oil traps powder and dust, which congeals into deposits that interfere with the safe and reliable operation of the revolver. On a gun with an open action, that is not theoretical.
steps.aside: Always and lastly, swab the interior of the barrels with cotton patch with gun oil to coat and protect the bore and chambers from rust and corrosion.
steps.quote: Avoid using too much oil as powder, dust or other foreign material may get trapped in the oil. This could lead to congealed deposits which may interfere with the safe and reliable operation of the revolver.
steps.cite: EAA Windicator Series Double Action Revolver — Warnings and Instruction Manual — Warnings and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — TO CLEAN AND MAINTAIN YOUR REVOLVER, printed pp.18-19

steps.title: How often, by EAA's own rule
steps.action: Clean it after firing, every time. Wipe the outside with an oiled cloth after handling even when it has not been fired. If it has been stored, take the excess oil back out before shooting.
steps.prose: The handling wipe matters more than it sounds on a blued revolver — fingerprints are acidic and they etch a visible print into blueing within days in a humid house.
steps.aside: If the gun has been stored, remove all excess oil and/or grease before firing.
steps.quote: A gun should be cleaned after firing. In addition, external parts should be wiped with an oiled cloth after handling.
steps.cite: EAA Windicator Series Double Action Revolver — Warnings and Instruction Manual — Warnings and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — TO CLEAN AND MAINTAIN YOUR REVOLVER, printed pp.18-19

steps.title: ⛔ Nothing was taken apart — and that is the manual
steps.action: Close the cylinder and check the bore and chambers are clear of patch material before anything else. EAA publishes no disassembly procedure for this revolver at all; the routine job is done with it assembled.
steps.prose: ⛔ EAA's position on going further is stated as a transfer of responsibility rather than a prohibition, which amounts to the same thing for an owner: whatever you take apart, the correct reassembly is on you.
steps.quote: THE GUN OWNER MUST ACCEPT FULL RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE CORRECT REASSEMBLY AND FUNCTIONING OF THE FIREARM AFTER ANY DISASSEMBLY OR REPLACEMENT OF PARTS.
steps.cite: EAA Windicator Series Double Action Revolver — Warnings and Instruction Manual — Warnings and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — TO CLEAN AND MAINTAIN YOUR REVOLVER, printed pp.18-19

deepAbsentReason: ⛔ EAA PUBLISHES NO DISASSEMBLY PROCEDURE FOR THIS REVOLVER. The manual's maintenance section is titled "TO CLEAN AND MAINTAIN YOUR REVOLVER" and runs eight lettered steps, of which the only one that opens anything is "Swing out cylinder." There is no sideplate step, no crane step, no grip step, and no parts-removal step anywhere in the book. What it does print is a transfer of responsibility — "THE GUN OWNER MUST ACCEPT FULL RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE CORRECT REASSEMBLY AND FUNCTIONING OF THE FIREARM AFTER ANY DISASSEMBLY OR REPLACEMENT OF PARTS" — plus an instruction to let a qualified gunsmith do the work. A deep clean authored here would be invention, and the exploded parts diagram is an ordering aid, not a procedure.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBERS
tasks: Brass bore brush and powder solvent, bore and every chamber
⛔ Oiled patch LAST, through bore and chambers

cleaning.name: FIRING WALL & CYLINDER
tasks: Powder fouling off the firing wall and the barrel's rear face
Front face of the cylinder — the blast ring
Small soft brush and solvent, then wipe the solvent off

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: ⛔ Wipe ALL excess solvent away before oiling — it attacks the bluing
A LIGHT coat of rust preventative, not a generous one
Wipe with an oiled cloth after handling, fired or not

reassembly: Nothing came apart, so there is nothing to rebuild.
Swing the cylinder closed and let the latch engage on its own — never flick it shut, which springs the crane.
Check the bore and every chamber for patch material or excess oil before ammunition appears.
Function check before the revolver goes away or is carried.
fncheck: Unloaded and every chamber seen empty, muzzle safe. Open and close the cylinder several times — it should drop in and latch without dragging. Cock the hammer and decock it under thumb control. Then work the action through a full double-action stroke slowly and watch the cylinder carry up and lock BEFORE the hammer falls. ⛔ Above all, check the trigger returns fully forward on its own after every stroke: EAA's own rule is that a trigger which does not return means the revolver is unloaded immediately and not used until it has been repaired.
